title: Connected Still Life
tagline: Maximize live cells in a stable, connected Game of Life pattern inside an n x n box.
description: Find a connected still life in an n x n bounding box with more live cells than the current record. For example, the best known connected still life in a 20 x 20 box has 148 live cells (37% density). Submit a 20 x 20 grid with 149 or more. A still life is a Game of Life configuration where no cell is born or dies. Connected means all live cells form one 8-adjacent component.
context: The maximum density of an unconstrained still life approaches 1/2. Requiring connectivity drops this because you cannot freely tile isolated stable pieces. For small n the optima are known. For n >= 16, the best-known patterns are from ad hoc searches and are likely suboptimal. The density gap between connected and unconstrained still lifes widens as n grows, making larger boxes the more interesting targets.

leaderboard.note: Records for connected still lifes. Sources: LifeWiki, Eppstein. Some values need verification.

verification: Checks Game of Life stability (every live cell has 2-3 neighbors, no dead cell has exactly 3) and 8-connectivity via BFS. O(n^2), milliseconds.

suggestedApproach.title: Start from known still lifes
suggestedApproach.body: Beehives, blocks, boats, loaves. Combine them into connected patterns. The hard part is making valid joins - most naive connections violate stability.

suggestedApproach.title: Simulated annealing
suggestedApproach.body: Score = live cells minus penalty for stability violations. Flip cells to improve. When penalty reaches zero, check if it beats the record.

suggestedApproach.title: SAT / MaxSAT
suggestedApproach.body: Encode stability and connectivity as boolean constraints. Maximize live cell count. Works well for n <= 20.

suggestedApproach.title: Target large n
suggestedApproach.body: n=32 has density 38.1% against a theoretical ceiling near 50%. Largest gap, most room for improvement.

agentPrompt: I want you to find a connected still life in Game of Life that fits inside a 20x20 bounding box and has more than 148 live cells. A still life means: every live cell has exactly 2 or 3 live neighbors (so it survives), and no dead cell has exactly 3 live neighbors (so none are born). Connected means all live cells are reachable from each other via 8-adjacency (including diagonals). Use a combination of SAT encoding and simulated annealing. Output the grid as a JSON array of arrays (0s and 1s), 20 rows of 20 values each.

bounds.name: Live cells: 2 or 3 neighbors
bounds.formula: Each live cell must have exactly 2 or 3 live neighbors to survive

bounds.name: Dead cells: not exactly 3
bounds.formula: No dead cell adjacent to the pattern may have exactly 3 live neighbors

bounds.name: 8-connected
bounds.formula: All live cells reachable from each other via edge or corner adjacency

bounds.name: Upper bound ~1/2
bounds.formula: Elkies (1998). Connected constraint reduces this to roughly 40-45% in practice.

references.text: Elkies, N. (1998). The still-life density problem. Voronoi's Impact on Modern Science, Book 2.
Eppstein, D. Blog posts on still life density.
